title: The Span — one fermion, two shores

steps.caption: Some things belong to no single place.
This forest is a quantum computer. So is every field past its fence.
A qubit holds both answers at once — but it lives HERE, and what lives somewhere can be reached.
A Majorana span: one fermion, split between two shores. Neither end holds the state — the PARITY between them does.
Braiding writes on it. S on this shore…
…√X on the far one. A Clifford alphabet, spelled across the map.
Noise must touch BOTH ends at once to hurt it — the bridge decoheres at the PRODUCT of its shores' leaks. Anchor one end at home and the Bath can never reach it.
Fusion. One question, asked once: even or odd? Born decides, surprisal pays — and the bridge is gone, because reading it was localizing it.
Every law of this world in one gesture: looking is paying, knowledge is extraction.
